label: Fair
corporate_parent: Home Depot exclusive house brand. Manufactured by undisclosed OEM — likely Foremost Groups / Globe Union Industrial Corp (Taiwan-based, manufactures for multiple US retailers). Home Depot does NOT manufacture anything.
manufacturing_location: China (likely Chaozhou or Foshan ceramics region — dominant global toilet manufacturing center). OEM identity not officially disclosed.
outlook_rationale: Home Depot backing ensures availability and distribution. Product quality is what it is — budget positioning with razor-thin margins. Home Depot private label strategy prioritizes price, not quality leadership.
platform_disclosure: Glacier Bay is a Home Depot exclusive private label brand likely manufactured by Foremost Groups / Globe Union Industrial Corp. The same OEM factories may produce toilets for other retailers under different brand names. No platform sharing with TOTO, Kohler, or American Standard — these are entirely separate manufacturing ecosystems.

construction.description: Two-piece, standard exposed trapway. Builder-grade construction. Minimum viable toilet.

glazing.description: Standard glaze only. No antimicrobial coating, no nano-barrier. Bowl staining and waste adhesion expected to worsen quickly vs CeFiONtect or EverClean-equipped toilets.

trapway.description: Partially glazed trapway. Rougher internal surface increases clogging risk. Standard 2" diameter.

china_body.description: Thin-wall economy grade china. Plumber reports of cracking under seat weight and during installation. Lower firing temperature than TOTO/Kohler. Less dense, less chip-resistant.

map_score.notes: MaP ~500g estimated. Many Glacier Bay models absent from MaP Testing database (itself a signal — brands submit voluntarily, and absence suggests scores may not be competitive). Below MaP PREMIUM 600g threshold. Spotty data.

performance_evidence.flush_technology: Standard gravity 2-inch flapper. Smallest standard flush valve. Slowest water delivery. Most basic flush mechanism available.
performance_evidence.water_efficiency: 1.28 GPF — WaterSense certified. Meets the legal minimum.
performance_evidence.bowl_cleanliness: Fair — standard rim-fed wash with no special rinse technology. No antimicrobial glaze. Weak rinse coverage leads to staining.
performance_evidence.noise: Standard. Can be noisier than premium due to valve quality.

flush_valve.description: Standard 2-inch rubber flapper. Shortest service life — 2-3 years before degradation. Frequent running toilet complaints. Universal $3-5 replacement.

fill_valve.description: Ships with Fluidmaster-compatible fill valve (may actually BE a Fluidmaster 400A). Universal replacement available. This is the one genuine bright spot.

parts_ecosystem.description: All parts are standard universal aftermarket. Fluidmaster fill valve, universal flapper, standard wax ring. Nothing proprietary. Easy and cheap to repair.

durability_evidence.diy_repairability: Fully DIY. Simplest possible repairs. All standard parts, all standard tools. BUT: you'll be repairing more frequently than premium toilets.
durability_evidence.warranty: 1 year limited. Minimal. Home Depot return policy (90 days) may be more useful than warranty.

sources.snippet: Glacier Bay models: limited/absent MaP data. Models that appear in database typically score 350-600g. Below MaP PREMIUM 600g threshold in many cases.
Builder-grade consensus: 'most service calls for clogs and valve failures.' Thin china, weak flush, running toilet complaints. Not recommended for quality installs.
Glacier Bay: 'you get what you pay for.' Cracking reports, running toilets, weak flushes. Plumbers see these on the most service calls. Builder-grade filler.
Universal Fluidmaster compatibility is the only durability bright spot. 2" rubber flapper = most frequent replacement part in all toilets. Budget parts meet minimum standards.
Budget toilets from Glacier Bay appear in some Consumer Reports tests. Performance varies widely by model. Not consistently recommended.

bottom_line: The Glacier Bay is a $100-150 builder-grade toilet. MaP scores below 600g PREMIUM threshold (when data exists — many models absent from database). 2-inch rubber flapper = shortest service life, most frequent running toilet complaints. Thin-wall china with cracking reports. No special glazing = staining. The ONLY bright spot is universal Fluidmaster parts compatibility — cheap and easy to repair, which you'll be doing frequently. Manufactured by undisclosed Chinese OEM for Home Depot. This is the floor of the market.
